parameters.description:
Passing a multi-row :class:`.Explanation` object creates a global
feature importance plot.

Passing a single row of an explanation (i.e. ``shap_values[0]``) creates
a local feature importance plot.

Passing a dictionary of Explanation objects will create a multiple-bar
plot with one bar type for each of the cohorts represented by the
explanation objects.
parameters.name: shap_values
parameters.type_doc: shap.Explanation or shap.Cohorts or dictionary of shap.Explanation objects

parameters.description: How many top features to include in the bar plot (default is 10).
parameters.name: max_display

parameters.description:
A function that returns a sort ordering given a matrix of SHAP values
and an axis, or a direct sample ordering given as a ``numpy.ndarray``.

By default, take the absolute value.
parameters.name: order

parameters.description: A partition tree, as returned by :func:`shap.utils.hclust`
parameters.name: clustering

parameters.description: Controls how much of the clustering structure is displayed.
parameters.name: clustering_cutoff

parameters.description:
Controls if data values are shown as part of the y tick labels. If
"auto", we show the data only when there are no transforms.
parameters.name: show_data

parameters.description: Axes object to draw the plot onto, otherwise uses the current Axes.
parameters.name: ax

parameters.description:
Whether :external+mpl:func:`matplotlib.pyplot.show()` is called before returning.
Setting this to ``False`` allows the plot
to be customized further after it has been created.
parameters.name: show

returns.description:
Returns the :external+mpl:class:`~matplotlib.axes.Axes` object with the plot drawn onto it. Only
returned if ``show=False``.

signature: bar(shap_values, max_display=10, order=shap.Explanation.abs, clustering=None, clustering_cutoff=0.5, show_data='auto', ax=None, show=True)
summary: Create a bar plot of a set of SHAP values.
